title: C-2 — Trace file record
description: JSONL. Line 1 is the header record; every subsequent line is one request. Token IDs are NOT stored — only content_seed. The materializer turns (content_seed, prompt_len, vocab_size) into an exact token sequence deterministically, which keeps traces small and diffable and makes the file portable to the simulator, which needs no token content at all. Regenerating a trace with the same seed and parameters MUST produce a byte-identical file (Week-1 test, not an assumption). Float formatting is the usual culprit: arrival_offset_s is fixed at 4 decimal places. The trace's SHA-256 is the identity used everywhere downstream.

trace_schema.description: Version gate. Loaders MUST reject unknown versions loudly rather than defaulting (§12.2).

arrival.description: F-16: seeded arrival process, Poisson with configurable burst structure.

priority_mix.description: F-16 requires a configurable priority mix. §5.4: `priority` is a PASSTHROUGH LABEL. It is generated (F-16) and carried through the trace and every log record, but no policy in §4.1 reads it and no priority-conditioned metric is reported. Keep emitting it — the field costs nothing and keeps the trace format stable for future work (§9) — but do not build anything that branches on it.

arrival_offset_s.description: Serialized at EXACTLY 4 decimal places. Byte-identical regeneration depends on this.

priority.description: 0 = interactive, 1 = background. §5.4: `priority` is a PASSTHROUGH LABEL. It is generated (F-16) and carried through the trace and every log record, but no policy in §4.1 reads it and no priority-conditioned metric is reported. Keep emitting it — the field costs nothing and keeps the trace format stable for future work (§9) — but do not build anything that branches on it.

admissibility.description: F-13: the (prompt, output) length range every pool node can serve within the timeout ceiling.
